newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sogedim plans to sell its Adidas stake.
newsitem.headline: Sogedim plans to sell its Adidas stake.

text.p: German sportswear maker Adidas AG said on Thursday that Sogedim SA, holding 26.1 percent of the group's capital, would put that stake up for sale.
Adidas said that its chief executive Robert Louis-Dreyfus and management board member Christian Tourres, have agreed to purchase 2,950,000 shares each through the offering.
The remaining 5,938,000 shares would be offered to other investors, Adidas said.

The shares will be offered to institutional investors worldwide and retail investors in Germany following an accelerated global tender with UBS Limited acting as global co-cordinator and bookrunner together with Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corporation, UBS said.
A syndicate will be formed. The price for the shares is expected to be announced on April 16 while marketing and bookbuilding will begin today.

Separately the company, known for its three-stripe logo, said it had posted 1.7 billion marks ($986.7 million) in turnover during the first quarter of this year and expected pre-tax profits for the quarter to total at least 235 million marks.
